'''Paul Adrian Negulescu''' is an American [[Cell biology|cell biologist]]. He is a Senior Vice President at American [[Pharmaceutical industry|pharmaceutical company]] [[Vertex Pharmaceuticals]]. He received the 2022 [[Shaw Prize|Shaw Prize in Life science and medicine]], together with [[Michael J. Welsh (biologist)|Michael J. Welsh]], for their work that uncovered the [[etiology]] of [[cystic fibrosis]] and developed effective [[medication]]s.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Press Release |url=https://www.shawprize.org/prizes-and-laureates/life-science-and-medicine/2022/press-relesae |access-date=October 12, 2022 |publisher=Shaw Prize Foundation |date=May 24, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221012140007/https://www.shawprize.org/prizes-and-laureates/life-science-and-medicine/2022/press-relesae |archive-date=October 12, 2022}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Negulescu was born in [[San Francisco]] to [[Immigrant generations#First generation|first-generation immigrants]] from [[Romania]]. His father was a [[Surgery|surgeon]],<ref name="autobio"/> and his grandfather, [[Constantin Vișoianu]], was a former [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Romania)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]] of Romania.<ref>{{cite news |title=Florica Visoianu Obituary |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/washingtonpost/name/florica-visoianu-obituary?id=5528520 |access-date=October 15, 2022 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=April 10, 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015155707/https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/washingtonpost/name/florica-visoianu-obituary?id=5528520 |archive-date=October 15, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Constantin Vișoianu, Romanian official, dies |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1994/01/05/constantin-visoianu-96-romanian-official-dies/db81322d-4afd-4e22-99ef-37cb4f107228/ |access-date=October 15, 2022 |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=January 5, 1994 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015160905/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1994/01/05/constantin-visoianu-96-romanian-official-dies/db81322d-4afd-4e22-99ef-37cb4f107228/ |archive-date=October 15, 2022}}</ref> He has a brother.<ref name="autobio"/>

Thanks to his childhood experience, he initially wanted to graduate with [[history]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. A third-year [[physiology]] class taught by [[Roger Y. Tsien]] had a great influence on Negulescu, who eventually graduated with a [[Double degree|dual degree]] in history and physiology in 1986. He then went on and studied [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in physiology under Terry Machen, completing it in 1990.<ref name="autobio"/>

== Career ==
Negulescu started his career as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and under Michael Cahalan at the [[University of California, Irvine]]. He was planning to move to the [[University of Connecticut]] when [[Roger Y. Tsien]] asked him to join a [[startup company]] he was forming called [[Aurora Biosciences]].<ref name="autobio"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kresge |first1=Nicole |last2=Simoni |first2=Robert D. |last3=Hill |first3=Robert L. |title=The Chemistry of Fluorescent Indicators: the Work of Roger Y. Tsien |journal=[[Journal of Biological Chemistry]] |date=2006 |volume=281 |issue=37 |pages=e29–e31 |doi=10.1016/S0021-9258(19)34942-7 |url=https://www.jbc.org/article/S0021-9258(19)34942-7/fulltext |access-date=October 15, 2022 |archive-date=October 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015163531/https://www.jbc.org/article/S0021-9258%2819%2934942-7/fulltext|doi-access=free }}</ref> Negulescu joined Aurora Biosciences in 1996 as one of the first employees.<ref name="warrenalpert">{{cite web |title=Paul Negulescu |url=https://warrenalpert.org/prize-recipients/paul-negulescu |publisher=[[Warren Alpert Foundation Prize|Warren Alpert Foundation]] |access-date=October 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015164423/https://warrenalpert.org/prize-recipients/paul-negulescu |archive-date=October 15, 2022}}</ref> He became Senior Vice President of Discovery Biology in 1999. When [[Vertex Pharmaceuticals]] acquired Aurora Biosciences in 2001,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pollack |first1=Andrew |title=TECHNOLOGY; Vertex Buys Biotechnology Rival for $592 Million |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/05/01/business/technology-vertex-buys-biotechnology-rival-for-592-million.html |access-date=October 16, 2022 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=May 1, 2001 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016144750/https://www.nytimes.com/2001/05/01/business/technology-vertex-buys-biotechnology-rival-for-592-million.html |archive-date=October 16, 2022}}</ref> he was appointed Senior Vice President of Research.<ref name="autobio"/> Negulescu has been leading the [[San Diego]] Research Center of Vertex Pharmaceuticals since 2003.<ref>{{cite web |title=Paul Negulescu, Ph.D. |url=https://www.vrtx.com/leadership/paul-negulescu-phd |publisher=[[Vertex Pharmaceuticals]] |access-date=May 8, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190508110513/https://www.vrtx.com/leadership/paul-negulescu-phd |archive-date=May 8, 2019}}</ref>

== Research ==
Negulescu's research focuses on the therapy of [[cystic fibrosis]]. Cystic fibrosis can be caused by any of the thousands of identified [[mutation]]s in the [[Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator|CFTR]] protein, an [[ion channel]] that allows [[Chloride|chloride ions]] to pass through. These mutations have been classified into Class I to V, with Class III mutations causing defective channel gates in CFTR despite normal expression of the protein.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Michal |last1=Shteinberg |first2=Iram J |last2=Haq |first3=Deepika |last3=Polineni |first4=Jane C |last4=Davies |title=Cystic fibrosis |journal=[[The Lancet]] |date=2021 |volume=397 |issue=10290 |pages=2195–2211 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(20)32542-3 |pmid=34090606 |s2cid=235327978 |url=https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(20)32542-3/fulltext |access-date=October 17, 2022|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Via [[high-throughput screening]], his team at [[Vertex Pharmaceuticals]] discovered [[ivacaftor]], a [[Small molecule|small-molecule]] [[potentiator]] that increases the probability that mutated CFTR gates will open.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Fredrick |last1=Van Goor |first2=Sabine |last2=Hadida |first3=Peter D. J. |last3=Grootenhuis |first4=Bill |last4=Burton |first5=Dong |last5=Cao |first6=Tim |last6=Neuberger |first7=Amanda |last7=Turnbull |first8=Ashvani |last8=Singh |first9=John |last9=Joubran |first10=Anna |last10=Hazlewood |first11=Jinglan |last11=Zhou |first12=Jason |last12=McCartney |first13=Vijayalaksmi |last13=Arumugam |first14=Caroline |last14=Decker |first15=Jennifer |last15=Yang |first16=Chris |last16=Young |first17=Eric R. |last17=Olson |first18=Jeffery J. |last18=Wine |first19=Raymond A. |last19=Frizzell |first22=Melissa |last22=Ashlock |first23=Paul |last23=Negulescu |title=Rescue of CF airway epithelial cell function in vitro by a CFTR potentiator, VX-770 |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]] |date=2009 |volume=106 |issue=44 |pages=18825–18830 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0904709106 |pmid=19846789 |pmc=2773991|bibcode=2009PNAS..10618825V |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first1=Lawrence |last1=Lin |first2=Sook Wah |last2=Yee |first3=Richard B. |last3=Kim |first4=Kathleen M. |last4=Giacomini |title=SLC transporters as therapeutic targets: emerging opportunities |journal=[[Nature Reviews Drug Discovery]] |date=2015 |volume=14 |issue=8 |pages=543–560 |doi=10.1038/nrd4626 |pmid=26111766 |pmc=4698371 }}</ref> Ivacaftor was approved by the [[Food and Drug Administration]] (FDA) for cystic fibrosis patients with one specific Class III mutation in 2012, and has since been approved for mutation classes as well.<ref name="annurev">{{cite journal |first1=Michael M. |last1=Rey |first2=Michael P. |last2=Bonk |first3=Denis |last3=Hadjiliadis |title=Cystic Fibrosis: Emerging Understanding and Therapies |journal=[[Annual Review of Medicine]] |date=2019 |volume=70 |pages=197–210 }}</ref> Of note, the expanded approval in 2017 was based solely on ''[[in vitro]]'' data, due to the small number of patients carrying those rare mutations making [[clinical trial]]s impossible.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kingwell |first1=Katie |title=FDA OKs first ''in vitro'' route to expanded approval |journal=Nature Reviews Drug Discovery |date=2017 |volume=16 |issue=9 |pages=591–592 |doi=10.1038/nrd.2017.140 |pmid=28860581 |s2cid=2421594 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nrd.2017.140 |access-date=October 17, 2022|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Negulescu also led the discovery of another cystic fibrosis drug, [[lumacaftor]], which is known as a "corrector" as it acts as a [[Chaperone (protein)|chaperone]] to help the CFTR protein fold correctly.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fiedorczuk |first1=Karol |last2=Chen |first2=Jue |title=Mechanism of CFTR correction by type I folding correctors |journal=[[Cell (journal)|Cell]] |date=2022 |volume=185 |issue=1 |pages=158–168 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2021.12.009 |pmid=34995514 |s2cid=235649986 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Thus, it can be used in patients with Class II mutations, which create [[misfold]]ed CFTR protein that cannot reaching the [[Cell membrane|cell surface]].<ref name="annurev"/> The most common Class II mutation is F508del.<ref>{{cite web |title=Types of CFTR Mutations |url=https://www.cff.org/research-clinical-trials/types-cftr-mutations |publisher=[[Cystic Fibrosis Foundation]] |access-date=October 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221018143639/https://www.cff.org/research-clinical-trials/types-cftr-mutations |archive-date=October 18, 2022}}</ref> Again with high-throughput screening, Negulescu and his team found that lumacaftor can correct F508del-mutated CFTR protein.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Fredrick |last1=Van Goor |first2=Sabine |last2=Hadida |first3=Peter D. J. |last3=Grootenhuis |first4=Bill |last4=Burton |first5=Jeffrey H. |last5=Stack |first6=Kimberly S. |last6=Straley |first7=Caroline J. |last7=Decker |first8=Mark |last8=Miller |first9=Jason |last9=McCartney |first10=Eric R. |last10=Olson |first11=Jeffrey J. |last11=Wine |first12=Ray A. |last12=Frizzell |first13=Melissa |last13=Ashlock |first14=Paul A. |last14=Negulescu |title=Correction of the F508del-CFTR protein processing defect in vitro by the investigational drug VX-809 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=2011 |volume=108 |issue=46 |pages=18843–18848 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1105787108 |pmid=21976485 |pmc=3219147 |bibcode=2011PNAS..10818843V |doi-access=free }}</ref> It was later found that the drug was not effective enough when administered on its own,<ref>{{cite journal |first1=J. P. |last1=Clancy |first2=Steven M. |last2=Rowe |first3=Frank J. |last3=Accurso |first4=Moira L. |last4=Aitken |first5=Raouf S. |last5=Amin |first6=Melissa A. |last6=Ashlock |first7=Manfred |last7=Ballmann |first8=Michael P. |last8=Boyle |first9=Inez |last9=Bronsveld |first10=Preston W. |last10=Campbell |first11=Kris |last11=De Boeck |first12=Scott H. |last12=Donaldson |first13=Henry L. |last13=Dorkin |first14=Jordan M. |last14=Dunitz |first15=Peter R. |last15=Durie |first16=Manu |last16=Jain |first17=Anissa |last17=Leonard |first18=Karen S. |last18=McCoy |first19=Richard B. |last19=Moss |first20=Joseph M. |last20=Pilewski |first21=Daniel B. |last21=Rosenbluth |first22=Ronald C. |last22=Rubenstein |first23=Michael S. |last23=Schechter |first24=Martyn |last24=Botfield |first25=Claudia L |last25=Ordoñez |first26=George T. |last26=Spencer-Green |first27=Laurent |last27=Vernillet |first28=Steve |last28=Wisseh |first29=Karl |last29=Yen |first30=Michael W. |last30=Konstan |title=Results of a phase IIa study of VX-809, an investigational CFTR corrector compound, in subjects with cystic fibrosis homozygous for the F508del-CFTR mutation |journal=[[Thorax (journal)|Thorax]] |date=2012 |volume=67 |issue=1 |pages=12–18 |doi=10.1136/thoraxjnl-2011-200393 |pmid=21825083 |url=https://thorax.bmj.com/content/67/1/12.long |access-date=October 19, 2022 |pmc=3746507 |archive-date=October 19, 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20221019031143/https://thorax.bmj.com/content/67/1/12}}</ref> but was so when administered together with ivacaftor.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Claire E. |last1=Wainwright |first2=J.
